title: Workflows, agents and who owns the control flow

items.stem: Control flow means who decides which step runs next. Which question tells you whether a design is a workflow or an agent?

options.text: Does the design give the language model tools to call?
Does the design use a language model at all?
Does code or the model decide the next step?
Does a request take more than one model call?

items.stem: In your assistant, the model drafts a reply to a student. Code then runs a check on the draft. If the check fails, code sends the draft back to the model, up to 3 times, and then sends the reply. How should this design be classified?

options.text: An agent, because it repeats steps in a loop
A workflow, because code decides whether and when to repeat
An agent, because the model rewrites the draft each time
Neither, because a retry loop makes it a hybrid of the two

items.stem: Which part of the makerspace assistant is the best candidate to build as a fixed workflow rather than an agent?

options.text: Answering a manual question: search, reread the results, and search again until the right page turns up
Diagnosing a failed print: ask the student questions and pick the next check from their answers
Planning a project: decide which machines, manuals and calendars to look at, based on a description
Booking a slot: read the machine and time, check the calendar, book if free, send a confirmation

items.stem: Your team builds the booking part as a fixed workflow. What do you give up by doing that, compared with an agent?

options.text: Handling requests whose steps nobody wrote into the code
Letting the model call tools such as check_calendar
Having a language model write the replies to students
Keeping the cost of each request predictable

items.stem: In one sentence, when is an agent a better fit than a fixed workflow?

Your assistant is an agent: the model picks which tool to call next. The team then adds a code rule that book_machine can run only after check_calendar has returned for that machine. Which statement describes who decides what?

options.text: The model decides every step, including the order of those two tools
Code decides every step, so the system is now a pure workflow
Code decides the order of those two tools, and the model decides the other steps
A system is either an agent or a workflow, so this design must be redone
